why: Every hand patch the estate applies to an installed DSH engine tree, with the exact command that applies and checks it. Read by dsh-update/lib/patches.mjs. An install of a new engine version must end with every entry here reporting present (check exit 0), and with no unregistered .bak-harness-* pair left unexplained. See P3170 and dsh-update/DELIVERY.md.

patches.note: One malformed tool call must not kill a whole turn. Found 2026-10-05; the patcher embeds the repair engine and refuses if the upstream anchor moved.

superseded.evidence: Measured 2026-10-20 on the 0.2.1 tree: the unguarded async settlement watcher this patch existed to catch is gone. dsh-subagent/lib/index.js now wraps EVERY lifecycle listener's returned promise in `Promise.resolve(returned).catch(...)` (line 171) and the settlement path is a defined `settle: ({stopReason, output})` handler (line 199) with `settlementSummary` / `createSettlementMessage` / `kind: "subagent-settled"`. lib/types/activation.js no longer contains an async IIFE at all, and the manager catches disposal promises at 1274/1306/1319/1363/1381. So on 0.2.1 this patch has nothing to add: its first target is already-hardened in our tree by an earlier partial apply, and its other two targets do not exist any more. On the 0.2.0 line it is still needed.

patches.note: A finished child agent must not die at settlement and lose its report. Found 2026-09-30.
Currency must render as text, not LaTeX. Found 2026-09-25. Targets the hashed vendor bundle, so it is resolved by glob, never by filename.

superseded.evidence: Measured 2026-10-20 in the installed 0.2.1 tree, dsh-client-ui-workspace/lib/client.js: the function this patch modified (`reuseOrCreateBlank`) no longer exists, and upstream now states and enforces the isolation it was written for — `sessionVisible()` contains `if (session.blank && session.id !== current) return false;` under the comment 'among blank sessions, only the current one is visible', and `pinCurrentBlank()` keeps the selected blank first without duplicating a slot. So a window no longer adopts another window's blank row. NOT PROVEN the way the patch was: this is a reading of the upstream code, not two windows opened side by side; the patch's own symptom was visual. On the 0.2.0 line the patcher still applies and is still needed.

patches.note: A second window must not reuse a blank workspace. Exit 4 means absent, 5 unverifiable (refuses on an unknown upstream).

Until a patcher exists, the install-time audit decides it mechanically: if the new tree's file equals the old PATCHED file, upstream adopted the change and nothing is lost; otherwise the install FAILS and names this file. What would close it: a scripted diff of the backup against the patched file, the hunk expressed as a patcher, and this entry promoted to kind=script.
